### What's New

**Your multi-bench instances now report each bench separately.**
`cwcli status` modeled one bench and asked `localhost:8000` about all of them, so a healthy second bench read as degraded and a bench serving nothing reported its neighbor's response as its own. cwcli now measures each bench on its own port and against its own site.

**Breaking: `cwcli axi status` moved its per-bench fields.**
`supervisor_up`, `web_http_code`, `processes`, and `not_cwcli_supervised` now live under `benches[i]`, on single-bench instances too. Anything reading them at the top of the document needs updating.

**Run more than six benches on one instance.**
A seventh bench used to bind its port inside the container and stay unreachable from your machine. `cwcli scale` widens the range of ports the instance publishes, and it leaves your database alone.

**A misspelled flag now stops the command instead of being ignored.**
`cwcli stop myproj --benhc 1` used to stop the whole instance and complain only that it could not find two projects. `start`, `stop`, `restart`, and `rm` now reject an option they do not recognize before they touch a project.

**Drop one site without destroying the instance.**
`cwcli rm-site` removes one named site and leaves the instance and every other site running. It also moves the database credentials that `bench drop-site` leaves sitting inside the container to a location you can manage.

**Bench commands that ask questions now work through `cwcli run`.**
`bench new-app`, `console`, and `mariadb` all prompt, and they used to fail on the first question. Pass `-i` and they work.

**`apps checkout` now protects uncommitted work, as the docs always claimed.**
It used to carry your local edits across a branch switch and report success. It now refuses and names the files it found, and `--reset` is still the way through.

**Your agents can delete instances, install apps, and build assets.**
`cwcli axi rm`, `cwcli axi apps install`, and `cwcli axi build` close the gaps where an agent previously had to fall back to a raw command. Each one keeps the safety rules its human command has.
